# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared PC Domain and Guest

Shared PC mode like [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared PC, but with a guest account as well: the sign-in screen shows a Guest button with which someone without an account starts a temporary local session.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Device config |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — Intune Shared multi-user device (sharedPCConfiguration, SharedPC CSP), variant of [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared PC with allowedAccounts guest,domain. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_PC_Domain_Guest.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Shared_PC_Domain_Guest.json) |

> Own group SG-D-UEM-WIN-SharedPC-Guest (assigned); see the note on [Baseline] - WIN - D - Shared PC for how the groups are divided — a device is in exactly one of the two Shared PC groups. A guest has no Entra identity: Conditional Access, MFA and Intune compliance do not apply to them, and they cannot reach the organisation's Teams, SharePoint or mail. That makes this a device for the internet and public services, not for work. What a guest can do is everything the device itself allows: do not open up sensitive shared folders or printers that are reachable without signing in. Mind the interaction with [Baseline] - WIN - D - User Rights: it denies local sign-in to the built-in Guests group (*S-1-5-32-546). Microsoft does not document which local group the Shared PC guest account lands in; test in the pilot whether the Guest button works. If it does not, that right is the cause and a tenant-specific copy of User Rights without that SID belongs on SG-D-UEM-WIN-SharedPC-Guest. [Baseline] - WIN - D - Local Security Policies also disables the built-in Guest account; that is a different account from the Shared PC guest and stays disabled.
